column3: “The son of a Jaminite man” is rendered “the son of a Benjamite,” and “mighty man of wealth” as “a mighty man of valor.”
“Young and good” is rendered “a choice and handsome man.”
“She-asses” is rendered “donkeys,” and “young men” as “servants.”
“And not there” is rendered “but they were not there,” and “land of the Jaminite” as “land of the Benjamites.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “to be concerned about.”
“All that he speaks surely comes” is rendered “surely comes true”; “tell us our way” becomes “tell us about our journey.”
“And behold, we will go” is rendered “But behold, if we go.”
“There is found in my hand” is rendered “I have in my hand.”
NASB puts the verse in parentheses; “the prophet of today” is rendered “he who is called a prophet now.”
“Your word is good” is rendered “Well said.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“There is; behold, before you” is rendered “He is; see, he is ahead of you.”
“As the day” (meaning “now”) is rendered “at once.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Uncovered the ear of Samuel” is rendered “revealed this to Samuel”; “this” is supplied.
“Ruler” is rendered “prince,” and “I have seen” as “I have regarded.”
“Yahweh answered him” is rendered “the LORD said to him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“All that is in your heart” is rendered “all that is on your mind.”
“Today three days” is rendered “three days ago,” and “set your heart” as “set your mind.”
Close to the Hebrew; “clans” is rendered “families.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“The thigh and what was on it” is rendered “the leg with what was on it”; NASB names “Samuel” as the speaker. The Hebrew of the last part is difficult and the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB names “Samuel” as the one who spoke.
“Outside” is rendered “into the street.”
“As the day” is rendered “now,” and “make you hear” as “proclaim … to you.”
